subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted workspace-agent discovery, or keep agent registration explicit through agents.list and agents.create/update/delete unless a narrower missing API is identified?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; it adds config surface, filesystem scanning, live routing semantics, and security trust boundaries that repository policy reserves for maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent-management RPCs, and document or improve that path before adding filesystem discovery.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Define a core discovery contract with trusted roots, file schema, conflict precedence, reload behavior, and security validation before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Or Tooling
options.body: Leave external workspace scanning to operator tooling or a plugin until a concrete missing OpenClaw extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent-management RPCs, and document or improve that path before adding filesystem discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger introduced the agent-list discovery tool and has the strongest history signal for deciding the model-visible multi-agent discovery boundary.
